Ava: Heads-up — during the onboarding flow for the Node sampleapp we saw request IDs disappearing and logs spamming at DEBUG even though SAMPLEAPP_LOG_LEVEL=info. Repro steps below, looks like an init ordering/race between our logger and the OpenTelemetry hooks.

Ava: Repro (simple):
1) git clone https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp-telemetry-repro
2) npm i && NODE_ENV=production SAMPLEAPP_LOG_LEVEL=info node server.js
3) hit /api/hello a few times (with retries)

Ava: Observed: request_id sometimes absent from later retry logs; top-level logs printed at DEBUG. Happens unpredictably 1/5 requests.

Ava: server.js init order is basically:
```js
// server.js
require('redwood-logger').init();
require('@opentelemetry/node').register(); // our OTel auto-instrumentation
const app = require('./app');
app.listen(3000);
```

Rohit: Which SDK versions and Node?

Ava: Node 18.16.0, redwood-logger 1.4.2, @redwood/telemetry 0.9.7 (OTel wrapper), express 4.18.2

Jamie: Sounds like hook ordering: if OTel patches console/express after our logger init it may reconfigure levels or replace transports. Also retries can re-run middleware where reqid gets reattached. Any logs/examples?

Ava: Yeah pasted a short trace:
```
INFO  [req=abc123] incoming request /api/hello
DEBUG [req=] retry attempt 2 fetch retry failed
INFO  [req=] fallback handler served
```

Marta: :eyes: Can you try flipping the import order (OTel first, logger second) as a quick test? If that fixes it we should patch the SDK to be resilient regardless of order.

Ava: Flipping order does reduce repro rate to ~1/30. So ordering matters. But we can't expect every app to import in a specific order.

Rohit: Likely root cause: our logger caches level & context at init time. OTel's auto-instrumentation monkey-patches things (like http/express) and can change environment-driven level at its init. If logger reads process.env once and OTel mutates or resets env/config later we get mismatch. For reqid: our request-id middleware is being wrapped and on retries the context propagation loses the header if the OTel wrapper re-invokes middleware differently.

Jamie: Workaround for customers: 1) require('@redwood/telemetry').register({ early: true }) before logger, or 2) set SAMPLEAPP_LOG_LEVEL in code to force at runtime: `logger.setLevel(process.env.SAMPLEAPP_LOG_LEVEL || 'info')`. But agree we need a proper fix.

Ava: I pushed a minimal repro branch and added a script `npm run repro-err` that spikes it quickly: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp-telemetry-repro/branch/ordering-repro

telemetry-bot: Created internal ticket DX-7429: "logger init ordering causes reqid loss & loglevel mismatch with OTel" and linked repo branch. CC @devex-team

Marta: Thanks — assigning to Rohit & Jamie. Please add a small integration test in the SDK to simulate OTel patching after logger init. Also include guidance in onboarding docs about recommended import patterns until we ship a fix.

Rohit: Proposed fix options:
- Make logger lazy-evaluate environment level on first log and listen for reconfig hooks from telemetry wrapper.
- Expose `logger.init({ defer: true })` and have telemetry register trigger final init.
- Ensure request-id middleware attaches to raw http layer instead of express layer so wrappers don't drop it.

Jamie: I can prototype lazy-eval level + a tiny middleware attach change this week. If we do lazy-eval we should still provide opt-in strict init for customers who want deterministic startup config.

Ava: For immediate mitigation, adding this to onboarding README would help: "If you use OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation, call telemetry.register() before logger.init() or call logger.setLevel(...) after your telemetry init."

Marta: Please also include an example snippet for serverless where ordering is trickier. Good catch.

Rohit: FWIW I reproduced a separate edge: if process.env.SAMPLEAPP_LOG_LEVEL is set via a config provider that updates env asynchronously (k8s secrets refresh) the cached level never updates. So lazy-eval also solves that.

Ava: Thanks — I'll link DX-7429 in the sampleapp branch and update the repro readme with the workaround. Will ping once we have a patch candidate. :thumbsup:

Jamie: Adding unit test ticket GH#3214 to the DX-7429 epic.

telemetry-bot: Ticket DX-7429 updated: assignees Rohit, Jamie; priority P2; status triage.
